content:
People magazine reported on Monday that Prince Harry is considering developing a documentary about his late mother, Princess Diana.

Multiple sources told the magazine that "Harry has also reached out to family members and friends connected to his late mother," but they stressed that "no documentary project has been finalised or confirmed at this stage."

The report came as the 30th anniversary of Princess Diana's death approaches.

The Princess of Wales was just 36 when she was killed in a high-speed car crash in Paris on 31 August 1997 while being pursued by paparazzi. Prince William was 15 at the time, and Prince Harry was only 12.

A source close to the Duke of Sussex told HuffPost that the royal has "discussed several potential projects" to mark the significant anniversary and is "still considering how best to honour her legacy."

There has long been speculation that the royal would undertake a project about his mother, ever since his deal with Netflix alongside Meghan Markle was first announced in 2020.

HuffPost has reached out separately to representatives for Prince Harry and to Kensington Palace; neither responded.

Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, previously announced he is releasing a new book to mark 30 years since his beloved sister's death.

The book, titled *Swan Song: Diana, My Sister*, will go on sale on 22 September.

In a press release announcing the new publication, Spencer said: "As the 30th anniversary of Diana's tragic death approaches, I have been inundated with requests to give interviews about my sister."

He continued: "This has prompted me to put my thoughts and memories down on paper once and for all, rather than risk subjecting myself again to the discomfort of reading others' commentary — much of which is based on lies that have, over time, come to be regarded as facts."

The historian added: "The purpose of this book is to speak about Diana from her brother's point of view, as I tried to do at her funeral. Like that tribute, I hope to speak about Diana with honesty and in a positive light."
